subject: Integration runway & MAP: finalizing tenant bootstrap and networking cadence
messages:
Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
From: Alex Morton <alex@clearbridgehealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@clearbridgehealth.com>
Subject: Re: Integration runway & MAP: initial questions on keys/peering

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — we liked the latency numbers. Before we schedule the onboarding call, our infra team asked for a concise checklist so we can scope tasks on our side. Specifically:

- How do we provision org-level access? Do you create an org/team inside Redwood or do we invite service accounts?
- API key model: do you recommend ephemeral keys for the POC or standard long-lived keys? Any TTLs/rotation guidance?
- IP allowlist: we need the exact CIDR/prefixes to add to our firewall and whether Redwood supports per-tenant allowlists vs global.
- VPC peering: is a managed peering option available or do we need to set up VPN/Terraform? Any sample configs?

Attached is our internal network diagram (redacted) to help — hope that helps.

Can we get a MAP-style checklist and a proposed timeline (2–3 week POC preferred)? Also, the security team will send a short questionnaire — I can forward when ready.

Thanks,
Alex Morton
Director, Platform Engineering
ClearBridge Health

Attachment: clearbridge_network_topology.pdf (PDF, 1 page, redacted)

Date: Sun, 08 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Subject: Re: Integration runway & MAP: draft MAP + POC connectivity checklist

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the diagram, that helps a lot. I put together a short MAP draft and the POC connectivity checklist (attached as a spreadsheet). High level below — proposing a 3-week runway we can compress to 2 if teams align.

Mutual Action Plan (MAP) — POC scope (summary)
- Goal: Validate latency/cost on our hosted inference for sample workloads, and prove seamless keying/peering across your staging tenant.
- Success criteria: <1.2s median token latency on 2x32-token sample, validated embeddings throughput >= 500 req/min, org-level audit logs available.

Key deliverables & owners
- Org setup: Redwood to seed tenant and invite ops@clearbridgehealth.com as Org Admin. (Owner: Olga) — Target: Day 1
- API keys: Provide short-lived API keys for evaluation + one long-lived service key for CI tasks. Recommend TTL = 24h for ephemeral keys; rotation via our console or API. (Owner: Ben) — Target: Day 1
- IP allowlist: Provide both public egress IPs (for outbound callbacks) and optional per-tenant allowlist. We'll supply a /24 block for managed endpoints; you can add it to firewall. (Owner: Neha) — Target: Day 2
- VPC peering: Support both managed peering and customer-initiated peering. For managed peering we exchange project IDs and create the connection; for customer-initiated we provide a Terraform snippet. (Owner: Ben) — Target: Day 3–5 (depends on cloud approval)
- Security questionnaire: We'll complete your questionnaire and attach SOC2 cover notes. (Owner: Marissa) — Target: Day 2

Timeline (proposed, 3-week cadence)
- Week 0 (prep): NDA, security questionnaire in -> 2 business days
- Week 1: Org + API keys + IP allowlist configured; smoke tests run
- Week 2: VPC peering or tunneled routing configured; performance tests
- Week 3: Acceptance criteria check and runbook handed off; optional extended evaluation

Notes / technical constraints
- Ephemeral keys: our SDKs support automatic refresh; recommend embedding the refresh endpoint behind your CI secrets manager for tests needing longer runs.
- Peer options: managed peering avoids changes on your routing tables — customer-initiated gives you full control if your security team requires.

I attached the MAP draft (spreadsheet) and put link to the HubSpot deal. If this looks good we can lock the timeline and schedule a 45-min onboarding for Monday or Tuesday next week.

Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_map_draft_v1.xlsx (XLSX)
Related links: https://hubspot.example/record/RDW-2391

Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 08:27:00 -0800
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Morton <alex@clearbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>
Subject: Re: Integration runway & MAP: technical notes on keys, IPs, and peering

Alex / Olga — quick technical addendum from my side. Forwarding the MAP draft above and adding recommended specifics so your infra team can start the firewall/peering request.

API keys
- Provisioning: Olga will seed a ClearBridge staging tenant. Ops email will be added as Org Admin.
- Key types:
  - Ephemeral (recommended for user-flow tests): generated via POST /orgs/{id}/keys?type=ephemeral; default TTL = 24h.
  - Service key (CI/automation): generated via POST /orgs/{id}/keys?type=service; no TTL but must be rotated per your policy.
- Rotation: We expose a key-rotation endpoint and a webhook for rotation events.

IP allowlist / public egress
- Managed endpoints: 34.72.128.0/24 (example public block) — add to your firewall for outbound callbacks.
- Per-tenant allowlist: yes — we can create a tenant-scoped allowlist (recommended). If you prefer, we can also provide an ephemeral NAT IP for short runs.

VPC peering options
- Managed peering (Redwood-managed): we handle cloud-side setup; you approve a peering request from your console. Timeline: ~48–72 hours.
- Customer-initiated peering: we provide a Terraform snippet and the required CIDR allocations. Example snippet (GCP-style):

  resource "google_compute_network_peering" "clearbridge-peering" {
    name = "rdw-clearbridge-peering"
    network = "projects/clearbridge-vpc/global/networks/clearbridge-vpc"
    peer_network = "projects/redwood-prod/global/networks/redwood-vpc"
    auto_create_routes = true
  }

- Routing: keep overlapping CIDRs disallowed; we’ll advise on acceptable ranges.

Next steps: I can join the onboarding call to walk through the terraform snippet and run a quick smoke ping test once keys are live.

Ben Carter
Staff Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
